topLine: The Minns government opened the $440 million Shoalhaven Memorial Hospital redevelopment at Nowra, with the Premier visiting the first patients, and separately announced safety works at a Princes Highway intersection south of Nowra — two tangible South Coast deliverables with obvious electoral salience. In commentary, Michelle Grattan argues on the ABC that One Nation's bigger test is in New South Wales rather than Victoria, with federal inflation pressures complicating Labor's position. Planning remains the other running theme, with the state proposing looser industrial land rules and local rezoning fights continuing in Kiama and Shellharbour.

In commentary, Michelle Grattan argues on the ABC that One Nation's bigger test is in New South Wales rather than Victoria, with federal inflation pressures complicating Labor's position. briefing.localWatch: Nowra's hospital redevelopment is now open and the government says it will improve the Princes Highway/Mortimer Road intersection at Falls Creek, south of Nowra. In Kiama, a rezoned 14.26-acre site at Caliope Street has been listed for sale amid what the Illawarra Mercury describes as community backlash.

stories.headline: Premier Chris Minns visits first patients in new $440m Shoalhaven hospital
stories.summary: Shoalhaven Memorial Hospital's $440 million redevelopment has officially opened, with the Premier visiting the first patients. The South Coast Register reports the seven-storey facility includes a regional pharmacy robot, while the government's release describes expanded facilities for the Illawarra and South Coast community.

stories.headline: Minns Labor Government to improve safety at Princes Highway and Mortimer Road intersection
stories.summary: The government has announced it will act to improve safety at the Princes Highway and Mortimer Road intersection at Falls Creek, south of Nowra, according to its ministerial release.

stories.headline: Controversially rezoned Kiama site hits the market amid community backlash
stories.summary: A 14.26-acre site at 2 Caliope Street, Kiama has been listed for sale after receiving rezoning approval, the Illawarra Mercury reports. The paper says the listing has come amid community backlash and that developers are moving to secure the parcel.

stories.headline: Council builds on reconciliation achievements
stories.summary: Shoalhaven City Council says it has completed all 48 actions in its inaugural Reflect Reconciliation Action Plan and is moving to the next stage, an Innovate Reconciliation Action Plan.

stories.headline: Minns Labor Government delivers simpler planning rules to power industrial growth
stories.summary: The government says it is proposing simpler and more flexible planning rules for industrial land across New South Wales, which it frames as a way to make better use of that land, attract investment and create jobs.

stories.headline: Port Kembla 'still a top pick' of sites for nuclear subs base ahead of inquiry report
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury reports that Peter Garrett, lead commissioner of a people's inquiry, told the paper Port Kembla remains a leading candidate site for a nuclear submarine base, ahead of the inquiry's report.

stories.headline: Not happy: the backflip that cost Shellharbour council millions of dollars
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury reports on a decision reversal that it says cost Shellharbour City Council millions of dollars. Council chief executive Wayde Peterson is quoted describing it as proof the council was "underfunded".

stories.headline: 'Determined to act': Residents rally to oppose Shellharbour rezoning proposal
stories.summary: Residents are organising opposition to a rezoning proposal at Shellharbour, the Illawarra Mercury reports, with one campaigner quoted saying an 83-year-old resident asked when a protest would be held.

stories.headline: Shellharbour council ignores police advice on alcohol-free zones
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury reports that a proposal to include alcohol-free zones in Shellharbour's New Year's Eve event was scrapped, despite police advice.

stories.headline: What's happened to The Grounds' plans for Lagoon restaurant site?
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury examines why the former Lagoon restaurant site remains empty, noting Wollongong City Council accepted the operator's tender almost a year ago.

stories.headline: One Nation might not win Victoria, but NSW is where the real fight is
stories.summary: Writing for the ABC, Michelle Grattan argues the more consequential contest with One Nation is in New South Wales rather than Victoria. She says NSW Labor has made plain how much of a threat it considers One Nation to be, and that the federal government's inflation troubles are compounding the problem.

stories.headline: Premier’s housing pattern book a blueprint for failure
stories.summary: A Daily Telegraph opinion piece criticises the Premier's housing pattern book, arguing it is failing to deliver. The full text was not accessible, so only the paper's headline framing is reported here.

elsewhere.text: Michelle Grattan writes that the Albanese government is telling voters cost-of-living pain will not ease soon, with Treasurer Jim Chalmers facing hard choices on inflation as the electorate's mood sours.
The Herald reports a $269,500 request for sewerage repairs at a Marrickville club has grown into a $6 million federal grant controversy involving the Prime Minister.
Ahead of Victoria's 28 November election, Victorian Labor has promised $893 million to fix 25 local roads, starting with works linking the Surf Coast Highway and Barwon Heads Road near Geelong.

Victoria's municipal association is pressing both major parties for a moratorium on data centres as planning approvals rise before next month's state election — a planning-politics fight worth watching in NSW.
The Conversation examines what Victoria's election means for treaty and Indigenous self-determination, noting recent gains sit precariously ahead of the 28 November poll.
In the Herald, a column reports former premier Jeff Kennett detecting arrogance in the Victorian Liberal leader, arguing the party has been slow to learn humility.
